vulnerabilities.description: Session memory files are written without restrictive permissions. Files are created world-readable (default mode 0o644), exposing sensitive session data. Use fs.writeFileSync with mode 0o600 or set permissions explicitly with fs.chmodSync().
Session files are written without restrictive permissions, exposing session data (working directory, metrics, context) to all users on the system. Sessions may contain sensitive information.
Archived session files are created with world-readable permissions. Archive historical data may contain sensitive context information.

Memory data stored in plaintext JSON format without encryption. If sensitive data like API keys, tokens, or credentials are stored via the set() command, they would be accessible in plaintext on disk.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Implement encryption using crypto module (AES-256-GCM) before storing sensitive data, or use a secure credential store.

vulnerabilities.description: Session context data is stored and retrieved in plaintext JSON. The context object can contain sensitive information that should be encrypted.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Encrypt sensitive context data before storing to disk, or implement secure session storage using encrypted cookies or secure databases.

vulnerabilities.description: JSON.parse() errors are silently caught and ignored. Corrupted memory files will silently return empty object without warning user, potentially losing critical state.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Log or warn about parse errors: } catch (e) { console.warn('Failed to parse memory file:', e.message); }

vulnerabilities.description: JSON.parse() errors are silently caught. Corrupted session files will silently return null without notifying the user, potentially causing session loss.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Log parse errors: catch(e) { console.warn('Failed to read session:', e.message); return null; }

vulnerabilities.description: The metric() function at line 115-121 doesn't validate the metric name before using it as an object key. Although JavaScript allows arbitrary keys, this could be exploited to manipulate session metrics or access unintended properties.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Validate metric names: if (!/^[a-z0-9_]+$/i.test(name) || !session.metrics.hasOwnProperty(name)) { console.error('Invalid metric'); return null; }

vulnerabilities.description: Regular expression patterns in TASK_PATTERNS lack anchors and could match unintended strings. For example, 'test' pattern could match 'attest' or 'testimony'.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Use word boundaries: '\\b(test|spec|coverage|unit test|integration)\\b' for better pattern matching.

vulnerabilities.description: No verification that 'gh' CLI command exists before attempting to use it. If GitHub CLI is not installed, cryptic error messages may appear.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Add pre-check: const { execSync } = require('child_process'); try { execSync('which gh'); } catch { console.error('GitHub CLI not found'); process.exit(1); }

summary.criticalIssues: Insecure file permissions on session/memory storage
summary.overallAssessment: The codebase has moderate security risks primarily related to file permissions and unencrypted storage of session data. The application is a static Next.js site without database or API endpoints, which significantly reduces attack surface. However, local file storage mechanisms (.claude/helpers) expose potential vulnerabilities if deployed in multi-user environments.

recommendations.description: All session and memory files must be created with mode 0o600 (read/write for owner only). Use fs.chmodSync() or native file creation options.
Implement AES-256-GCM encryption for memory and session context using Node.js crypto module. Create an encryption/decryption wrapper.
Replace silent error catching with proper logging. Add console.warn() or structured logging for JSON parse failures and file read errors.
Validate metric names in session.metric() function before using as object keys. Implement whitelist of allowed metrics.
Add word boundaries to pattern matching in router.js for more precise task classification.
Add existence checks for required CLI tools (gh, git) before use in helper scripts.

architecture.comments: This is a pure static calculator website with no backend, no authentication, and no database. XSS and SQL injection risks are minimal. Primary risks are from local file storage mechanisms and build-time operations.
